name: Matcha green drink routine

card.summary: A morning routine of whisked matcha or a greens drink that people pair with training and clean eating for energy and general health.

quick.overview:
Matcha is a powder of shade-grown green tea leaves whisked into water. Morning "green drink" routines use matcha or a greens powder as a ritual alongside breakfast and supplements.

The idea is that a plant-rich, low-sugar start to the day supports energy, diet quality and the lean, clear-skinned look many people want.
quick.how: It is prepared by whisking powder into hot water or blending with milk, and appears in forum breakfast lists next to eggs, oats, fish oil and greens powders.
quick.risks: Matcha contains caffeine, and shading may raise oxalate content compared with unshaded teas.

lead: Matcha is finely ground powder from shade-grown tea leaves, usually whisked into hot water, with Chinese roots and modern form developed in Japan.[1] Shading for two to three weeks raises caffeine and theanine and reduces catechin buildup.[1]
Lifters on T Nation have listed greens powders with matcha tea in breakfast posts alongside eggs, oats and fish oil.[2]

chain: Support for training and skin health (claimed)
angle.text: Users fold matcha into healthy-eating routines to support training and diet quality. Effects on appearance are unmeasured.

infobox: Chinese powdered tea; modern form Japan

paras: Leaves are steamed, dried into tencha, aged and stone-milled.[1] It contains polyphenols, including chlorogenic acid, and oxalates, possibly higher in shaded tea.[1]
A 2006 T Nation thread has a user listing a greens serving with matcha tea in a breakfast.[2]
No studies found on a matcha green drink routine and appearance.
